title: fix(console): docs ToC click jumps to home under <base href>
body:
## Problem

On a metadata-docs page (`/apps/:pkg/docs/:name`), clicking an entry in the right-side **本页目录 / On this page** ToC navigates to the **home page** instead of scrolling to the heading.

## Root cause

When the console is served under a sub-path, the host (`@objectstack/framework`, `packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts`) injects `<base href="…/_console/">` into the HTML. This is intentional and required — it lets relative asset URLs (`./assets/...`) resolve and lets React Router derive its `basename` from `document.baseURI`.

Side effect (per the HTML spec): with a `<base>` tag, **fragment-only** links resolve against the *base URL*, not the current page. So `DocPage`'s ToC anchors `<a href="#id">` navigate the browser to `/_console/#id` — whose pathname `/` is, under the `/_console` basename, the **home route**.

The same trap hits in-body markdown fragment links like `[x](#section)` (the existing content-click handler only intercepted `/docs/` links).

## Fix

`<base>` is load-bearing and can't be removed, so handle fragment navigation in JS:

- Add `scrollToHeading(id)` — `scrollIntoView` + `history.replaceState` writing an **absolute** path (`location.pathname + search + #id`), which ignores `<base>`.
- ToC anchors get an `onClick` that calls it (bare `href="#id"` kept for a11y / modified-click).
- `onContentClick` now also routes `#section` body links through the same helper.

No behavioural change when no `<base>` tag is present.

## Test

- [ ] Serve console under `/_console/`, open a long doc, click a ToC item → page scrolls to the heading, URL becomes `…/docs/<name>#<id>`, no home redirect.
- [ ] In-body `[x](#section)` link → same scroll behaviour.
